scope_note: Three conditional translation-anchoring routes. German renderer labels and source-history analogies are not gold. No registry addition, experiment selection, new data, image access, or readiness claim.

routes.title: Process invariant: operand, transformation, resulting state
routes.mechanism: Joint physical-process interpretation combining material/state transitions, quantity fields, and operation candidates across complete local records; it seeks a semantic relation among three roles rather than a word-frequency or position count.

exact_observation.quote:
### `ol`: R05 field relation, not yet a preparation noun

The current atlas contains 376 reader-exact `ol` occurrences. Nine immediate exact amount contacts occur on eight pages and are nearly symmetric around the target. Repeated `ol` field sequences, together with the fact that 58 of 59 apparent line-edge positions remain embedded in continuing records, fit a small relation that travels with a field better than a fixed liquid name. In `f58r.13`, `ol` joins a dry-state field to an independent process field; in `f3r.19`, it joins a cold-dry portion to a dry form. The least committal useful rendering is therefore contextual `und/mit`, with `von/aus` available in an amount attachment.

These local frames justify keeping the relation as the most useful reader default, but they do not produce a role win. R05, R01, and R03 each pass their gates with the same role score of 1.0; R05 is selected only because its dispatch priority is more specific. R01 *Ansatz/Zubereitungsbasis* and R03 measurable product/result are supported rivals, not failed alternatives. Confidence is therefore `C1_LOCAL_FRAME__C0_ROLE_TIEBREAK`. The form is extremely frequent, repetition is not exceptional among frequent forms, and its local environments are broad. Nothing distinguishes plant juice, extract, decoction, medicinal water, oil, wine, or vinegar. Visible similarity between EVA `ol` and Latin *oleum* earns zero identity credit.

candidate_plaintext_commitments: conditional: “combine/make [operand] into [result]” for an operation form only when the same record supplies a bounded operand and a resulting state
conditional: “with/by [relation]” for the recurrent field relation, without deciding whether the relatum is liquid, preparation, or product
routes.rival_countermodel: Independent recipe-record fields or copied templates can place amount, state, and operation near one another without asserting one physical transformation; a single form can be a noun, relation, or operation by local frame.
routes.held_prediction: On a predeclared set of complete records, a process reading must predict the same operand→operation→result relation across at least two source-bound frames, while the independent-field model permits operand and result to vary without a stable transformation. A failed conjunction leaves the route as structural context only.
routes.smallest_20min_step: Use already admitted/cached complete contexts for two GDT769 loci and one additional reader-exact `ckhy` or `ol/ols` frame. Blindly label only operand present, operation candidate present, result/state present, and same-record order; compare the two finite rival tables. No new translation or page reading.
routes.missing_binding: No independent English semantic endpoint currently binds the operation or material. GDT769 explicitly says role defaults are renderer choices and no liquid identity follows.
predecessors_and_difference: GDT769 is a role-dispatch audit with tied rivals; this route is a joint physical conjunction that can fail if no complete transformation relation recurs.
GDT783 HOT/DRY is a state-label rival, not an operand→process→result commitment.
routes.decision_change: A replicated conjunction would justify testing a small process clause against local alternatives; failure keeps all readings at C0 and prevents translating the operator.

routes.title: Value-field anchoring without assuming what X means
routes.mechanism: Treat the repeated H1–X–daiin construction as a candidate compositional semantic frame: X selects a kind of value-bearing field, while the following form contributes a bounded value. The hypothesis is about field/value semantics, not inherited German names such as quality, material, or stage.

exact_observation.quote:
# GDT877 — Four raw construction anchors; one annotation qualification

Four of the five fixed GDT764 H1–X–daiin constructions consist of three consecutive literal raw groups with definite internal spaces in all three readings. The fifth also has three consecutive groups and definite internal separators, but its ZL third group is `<!gap>daiin`; only its IT and RF readings meet the literal-whole criterion. This preserves four all-reading raw anchors and precisely qualifies the fifth. It does not establish their grammatical or numerical interpretation.

| Locus | Frozen construction | ZL | IT | RF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f105r.24 | pcheey dal daiin | Exact/clear | Exact/clear | Exact/clear |
| f105v.5 | pchedal qopchdy daiin | Exact/clear | Exact/clear | Exact/clear |
| f10v.1 | pcheey qoty daiin | Exact/clear | Exact/clear | Exact/clear |
| f22r.4 | pchaiin ofchy daiin | Exact/clear | Exact/clear | Exact/clear |
| f99r.15 | pcheody oteody daiin | Annotated raw group | Exact/clear | Exact/clear |

All fifteen complete raw-fragment lines match their corresponding cleaned cross-transcription lines before classification. Every pattern has one unique cleaned match in each reading. All fifteen matches map to three distinct consecutive raw groups, with definite internal separators; fourteen meet literal equality. There are no missing or ambiguous matches in this fixed set. The ZL annotation is retained exactly; this pass does not interpret it as a native physical gap or adjudicate a glyph. Its presence is a source qualification, not proof that the construction is absent or that an author wrote different words.

secondary_observation.quote:
All five triples are reader-exact, stand on paragraph-start lines, and are not
paragraph-final. Three lines contain a second `Y daiin` cell. The clearest is:

```text
pchedal | qopchdy daiin | chedy daiin | ...
```

That is field parallelism, not a plausible place to import an imperative. It
selects nominal syntax; it does not identify the field axis.

candidate_plaintext_commitments: conditional: “the following field has value III”
only if independently supported: “X selects a value domain” rather than “X means quality/material/result”
routes.rival_countermodel: H1–X–daiin is a copied layout or line-ending formula; `daiin` may be a delimiter or repeated token and X may be a label with no compositional value semantics. The exact raw construction alone cannot choose the rival.
routes.held_prediction: Across held reader-exact occurrences, a field model predicts that changing X changes the allowed value-domain/context while preserving the X–daiin relation; a copied-template model predicts no predeclared domain contrast. The test must use only an independently defined value/quantity endpoint, not the German glosses in GDT764.
routes.smallest_20min_step: Build a two-column hand-audit from the existing five fixed triples: construction identity and independently observable neighboring value/quantity marker. Predeclare one held contrast (e.g. repeated value marker vs no value marker) before viewing outcomes; do not infer III or any word translation from the current renderer.
routes.missing_binding: GDT877 establishes raw fidelity only; GDT764 supplies working axes and explicitly leaves three axes open. An independent value-domain marker is not yet available for all five triples.
predecessors_and_difference: GDT764 already proposes portable renderings; this route strips those labels and tests the narrower field/value compositional commitment.
GDT877 is a source-fidelity control, not a semantic result; it supplies the exact anchor but cannot itself confirm the route.
routes.decision_change: Success would create a finite semantic frame usable to anchor one clause while leaving X and daiin lexemes unresolved; failure blocks compositional translation and preserves the copied-template rival.

routes.title: Functional reference prose for paired local instruments
routes.mechanism: Use the admitted diagram-plus-text context to anchor a functional clause (“read one local wheel/field under its own register”) rather than naming stars, months, or German owners. The two-wheel independence is a constrained physical/document use hypothesis.

exact_observation.quote:
### f67r2 — PAIRED_BUT_DISCONNECTED_CELESTIAL_REFERENCE_WHEELS

**Arbeitslesung:** Zwei getrennte Himmelsräder: rechts ein zwölfteiliger Zeichen-/Kalenderrahmen mit eigenen Ring- und Bedingungsfeldern, links ein Stern-/Strahlenrad mit lokalen Innen- und Außenplätzen. Beide werden nebeneinander kopiert, aber nicht miteinander verrechnet.

candidate_plaintext_commitments: conditional: “the right and left instruments are consulted separately”
no commitment to any sign, planet, month, or word-to-glyph identity
routes.rival_countermodel: The two discs are decorative or copied teaching diagrams; nearby text may be generic prose and need not encode a lookup operation. A shared reference system could also link the wheels despite their visual separation.
routes.held_prediction: If the functional-reference hypothesis is right, existing text-side records assigned to the two local namespaces should show separable operand sets or operations, with no cross-wheel computation; the decorative/shared-reference rivals allow either no text correlation or a reproducible cross-wheel relation. A mismatch is a failure of this functional clause, not a refutation of the drawings.
routes.smallest_20min_step: Select two already admitted text records whose source assignment is independently documented near the f67r2 diagram and classify only namespace, explicit action/lookup language, and cross-wheel linkage. Compare the predeclared separate-lookup and shared-reference tables; do not inspect new images or assign planet/month names.
routes.missing_binding: V75 R2 is an authored working model, not independent proof of a functional text mapping; current SEM cards preserve related multilayer/local-namespace models but not this exact 74-application proposition.
predecessors_and_difference: V75 R2 provides the paired-but-disconnected instrument observation; this route asks for a text-side functional consequence, not another geometry or position count.
GDT876 corrects two written positions but does not decide the paired-wheel meaning; no target result is used here.
routes.decision_change: A replicated separate-lookup relation would supply a narrow functional plaintext anchor; absent that relation, retain the model as diagram context and do not translate neighboring text.

global_stop: Stop if any route requires inherited German roles as labels, unheld image interpretation, a global word-frequency effect, or treating a renderer output as an independent semantic binding.
